title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 384 (Debentures, annual return, registration of charges, books of account and their inspection)

content.overview: The provisions of section 71 apply mutatis mutandis to a foreign company. The provisions of section 92 and section 135 apply to a foreign company, subject to such exceptions, modifications and adaptations as may be made by rules, as they apply to a company incorporated in India. The provisions of section 128 apply to a foreign company to the extent of requiring it to keep at its principal place of business in India the books of account referred to in that section with respect to monies received and spent, sales and purchases made, and assets and liabilities, in the course of or in relation to its business in India. The provisions of Chapter VI apply mutatis mutandis to charges on properties created or acquired by any foreign company. The provisions of Chapter XIV apply mutatis mutandis to the Indian business of a foreign company as they apply to a company incorporated in India.
content.glance: s. 71 (debentures), s. 92/135 (annual return/CSR), s. 128 (books for Indian business), Chapter VI (charges) and Chapter XIV (inspection) apply to foreign companies as the section directs.
content.study: Section 384 extends selected Companies Act provisions to foreign companies. Debentures (s. 71) apply mutatis mutandis. Annual return (s. 92) and CSR (s. 135) apply subject to rule-based exceptions and modifications. Books of account under s. 128 must be kept at the principal place of business in India for Indian-business receipts, expenditure, sales, purchases, assets and liabilities. Chapter VI charge provisions apply mutatis mutandis to charges on property created or acquired by the foreign company. Chapter XIV inspection and investigation provisions apply mutatis mutandis to the Indian business.

sections.heading: Rule
sections.body: s. 71, s. 92/135, s. 128 (Indian business books), Chapter VI charges and Chapter XIV inspection apply to foreign companies as directed.

hypotheticals.question: What is the core effect of s. 384?
hypotheticals.analysis: It applies selected Act provisions (debentures, annual return, books, charges, inspection) to foreign companies for their Indian operations.

rows.left: Application of selected Act provisions to foreign companies

misconceptions.trap: Assuming every Companies Act provision applies automatically to a foreign company.
misconceptions.correction: s. 384 applies only the provisions it names, and only to the extent and with the adaptations it states.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should s. 384 be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify which subsection applies. II. Apply the named provision mutatis mutandis or as adapted. III. Limit the analysis to Indian business where the section so provides.
